name: @example/user-status
title: User Status Tile
description: Plugin tile of the dashboards proof of concept (stage E2): lists the users with status and groups. It uses @wippy/dashboards-tile-helper (from the wippy/dashboards module) for the tile protocol and writes only its rendering.

wippy.description: Dashboard tile (plugin 2 of the dashboards proof of concept) that lists every user with name, status and groups. It is not used by hand: the dashboard board (dashboard-layout) creates it and sets the tile_v1 attributes (tile-id, data-sources, actions, fields, options, params, mode) and, last, request-id. Input `main` has the shape `schema`: { users: [ { user_id, name, status, groups } ] }. The tile reads the data itself, reads it again when the live signal dash.users.changed arrives, and reports render-state (loading, computing, ready, empty, denied, error) to the board. Data that does not match the schema is reported as an error, never drawn.

request-id.description: A new id for each configuration. The board sets it last, and the tile starts work only when it is set.

data-sources.description: Map from input name to { url, args, refresh_ms, live_topic }. user-status reads the input main.

actions.description: Map from action name to { url, confirm }. Stage E3 adds the action set_status.

fields.description: Map from the tile field names to data field names. user-status has none.

params.description: Current values of the page parameters the tile declares.

mode.description: view (the POC has no edit mode).
